turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so we have twenty-five minutes, and I'd like to start with who decided Owen gets a zero, and why nobody called me before he read it on his phone in the middle of class.
Owen talks about you in class, by the way.
That's not what I asked, Hale. Who entered the zero, and on what basis?
He's one of the kindest kids I teach. He walked a new student around the building all through September.
Then why does he have a zero? Don't manage me, Hale. I've asked you twice now, and I'm writing down that I still don't have an answer.
A kid like that doesn't cheat out of malice. He was overwhelmed. We can both agree on that, right?
No, we can't. You just said "cheat" about my son with nothing on the table, and you're leading me to agree to it; I've spent twenty years watching people try that. What do you actually have, Hale?
